title: Chapter 58
content:
Several hours had passed since Jakyeong had been locked in the subterranean suite.

At first, he had expected someone to come down, but no matter how long he waited, not a single shadow appeared. Losing patience, he slipped into the master bath to inspect the perimeter. Noting that it was the only space without a dome camera overhead, he stepped onto the rim of the marble tub, bracing his palms against the heavy ceiling exhaust fan to shove it upward.

The vent didn't budge a millimeter.

He darted into the adjoining kitchenette, returned with a heavy serrated steak knife, and jammed the blade into the seam to pry the housing loose. But the reinforced plate had been locked down with tamper-proof security screws; it held completely fast.

Defeated, he surrendered with a furious huff, sliding down against the tile and letting his head fall back against the wall.

Damn it.

If you're going to keep me locked in a cage, the least you could do is leave me a pack of cigarettes. The refrigerator was packed to the brim with gourmet provisions, yet there wasn't a single lighter or smoke in sight. Trapped underground without nicotine was driving him up the wall. And knowing the psycho who owned the house, he refused to touch a single bite of the food, suspecting every container was laced with another dose of paralytic.

Pacing back into the lounge, he cracked open a sealed bottle of mineral water, took a measured gulp, and exhaled a long, frustrated breath.

He marched down the corridor to the elevator shaft, wedging his fingers into the seam of the outer steel doors and hauling them open with raw physical force. The cabin was parked on the upper floor. There was no way up; climbing the high-tension cables meant risking instant crushing if the lift engaged from above.

"Hey! Director Kang!"

His shout echoed loudly through the hollow concrete shaft. It was loud enough to carry upstairs, yet the estate remained dead quiet.

He cupped his hands, screaming at the top of his lungs:

"Let me out of here, you son of a bitch!"

"You sick, perverted bastard!"

"Fucking psychopath!"

"I hope lightning splits your skull open!"

"At least give me a fucking cigarette! A cigarette!"

He shrieked until his vocal cords burned, but the shaft answered with absolute, mocking silence.

God, this is infuriating.

Rubbing the tense cords of his neck, he trudged back toward the bedroom. Fuck. Does he plan on keeping me as some underground pet? Or does he genuinely intend to taxidermy my corpse? Knowing that unhinged demon, neither option was off the table.

He'd probably mount my stuffed corpse on a pedestal in his master suite just to jerk off to it every night.

Halfway down the hall, a sudden spark of cunning crossed his mind. Clasping a hand to his brow, he feigned a sudden, violent dizzy spell, swayed dramatically, and collapsed flat onto the polished tile. He kept his eyes shut, lying completely motionless in the center of the corridor.

If someone's watching those lenses, they'll have to send someone down to check.

Sitting propped against his headboard upstairs, watching the private CCTV feed on his flat-screen monitor, Il-hyun couldn't wipe the grin from his face.

Like a freshly landed fish thrashing on the dock, Lee Ja-kyeong had spent the last four hours pacing relentlessly—collapsing onto the mattress, tearing through the bathroom, stomping down the hallway, refusing to sit still for a single minute. The sheer, suffocating frustration radiating from the boy was palpable even through the digital screen.

Watching him pry the elevator doors apart and scream bloody murder into the shaft had provided top-tier entertainment.

Then, halfway down the corridor, the kid suddenly threw a hand over his face and took a dramatic, theatrical dive onto the floor.

Il-hyun’s brow arched. The boy lay there like a stiff corpse, not twitching a muscle.

Moments later, his bedside phone chimed.

[President Kang. The security center just flagged an alert. It appears Lee Ja-kyeong has collapsed—should we deploy a medical team?]

Studying the exaggerated splay of the boy's limbs, Il-hyun let out a quiet scoff.

"Leave him be. He'll get up on his own in a minute."

Ending the call, Il-hyun rested his chin on his knuckles, keeping his eyes glued to the display.

Ten minutes crawled by. Then twenty.

Suddenly, Ja-kyeong snapped upright, glaring straight into the nearest camera dome. With vicious, unvarnished venom, the boy thrust a stiff middle finger directly at the lens.

Il-hyun threw his head back, letting out a low, breathless laugh. His acting truly is god-awful.

On screen, Ja-kyeong grabbed another bottle of water, downed half of it, and retreated into the bedroom. Aside from the sealed factory water, he hadn't touched a single morsel of the prepared food. He tossed and turned across the mattress for several minutes before curling into a tight, defensive ball, his breathing finally leveling out.

Asleep for real this time.

Il-hyun stared at the sleeping silhouette for a long, quiet while. He hadn't realized observing another person could be this captivating. Maybe I really should keep him locked down there forever.

When he had dressed the unconscious boy in fresh loungewear after sedating him in the rain, suppressing his impulses had taken monumental restraint. Fighting the urge to taste that skin, to drive into that tight heat, to claim that defiant mouth... it had been a grueling trial of willpower.

He had indulged just enough to leave a few bruised teeth marks across the kid's nipples. If he noticed them when he woke, he's probably plotting my murder.

How to handle Lee Ja-kyeong going forward required careful calculation.

Il-hyun murmured softly toward the glowing monitor:

"Sleep well."

The screen flickered black with a tap of the remote. Il-hyun slid beneath the duvet and closed his eyes, though he knew peaceful sleep would be elusive tonight.

"Still nothing?"

"Yes, sir. He has entirely refused even water today."

Returning to the estate after hours, Il-hyun was briefed that Ja-kyeong had gone on an absolute hunger strike. It was now the fourth day.

On day one, the boy had thrashed and cursed; from day two onward, he had retreated into eerie, stone-still silence, refusing to leave the mattress. Up until yesterday, he had at least consumed bottled water, but today he hadn't touched a drop.

Unknotting his tie, Il-hyun switched on the master monitor.

The subterranean suite initialized on screen. Just as Tae-soo had reported, Ja-kyeong lay curled beneath the sheets, completely motionless—the exact same posture he had held since dawn.

"Have the housekeeper plate a fresh dinner tray."

Tae-soo hesitated. "Are you heading down personally, President Kang?"

"Yes."

"Allow me to accompany you."

"No need. Just have the tray ready."

"Understood, sir."

Once Tae-soo withdrew, Il-hyun lingered before the screen for a brief moment before heading to the kitchen. Taking the heavy silver tray from the housekeeper, he keyed the private elevator down to the subterranean level.

The heavy crunch of his dress shoes echoed down the barren concrete hallway.

Following the assassination attempt a year ago, the entire underground facility had been cleared of tactical hardware. Had he left the armory or the firing range intact, Ja-kyeong would have spent the last four days using armor-piercing rounds to chew through the ceiling.

Reaching the suite at the far end of the corridor, Il-hyun found the boy lying with his back to the door.

Even with the heavy footfalls crossing the threshold, Ja-kyeong didn't stir. Il-hyun set the tray down on the bedside table, taking a seat on the edge of the mattress and studying the curve of the boy's spine.

"Care for a smoke?"

The word smoke triggered an instant reaction.

Ja-kyeong rolled onto his back, blinking up with heavy, half-lidded eyes. His dark hair was a tousled, messy nest from days in bed, giving him an unexpectedly boyish, unguarded look.

When Ja-kyeong reached a hand out, Il-hyun moved to retrieve his silver cigarette case from his breast pocket—only for Ja-kyeong to give a slow, delicate shake of his head.

"No... Hold me," Ja-kyeong whispered, his voice thick with sleep. "It's been so long."

Il-hyun’s dark brow arched. Asking to be held with that dazed, innocent face?

He knew the kid was cooking up a lethal scheme, but with that slender hand lingering in the air, Il-hyun decided to play along. He leaned his broad frame over the bed, offering his chest without resistance.

Ja-kyeong’s arms looped around his neck, pulling him down until their lips collided in a bruising press.

Il-hyun’s eyes widened slightly. A hot, slick tongue breached his lips, exploring with aggressive heat. A scalding pulse flared straight to his groin. Il-hyun slid a large hand beneath the hem of Ja-kyeong’s shirt, fingers moving to knead the bare chest—

Snap.

The silk tie around Il-hyun's collar was expertly unlooped.

Before Il-hyun could pull back, Ja-kyeong whipped the heavy silk around Il-hyun's throat, rolled across the opposite side of the mattress, and hauled the fabric taut with all his body weight.

The garrote locked around his windpipe. A strangled, choking rasp tore from Il-hyun's chest as the arterial blood vessels along his temples and neck swelled into violent, throbbing cords.

Il-hyun clawed at his throat, trying to wedge his fingers beneath the silk, but Ja-kyeong braced his knees against the mattress frame, giving zero leverage.

Pivoting his entire upper body, Il-hyun threw his weight toward Ja-kyeong, dragging both of them off the bed in a concussive crash onto the hardwood floor.

The impact jarred the hold just enough for the silk to slacken. Il-hyun seized the opening, ripping the makeshift garrote from his throat with a violent yank.

Ja-kyeong vaulted to his feet, stepping back into a low combat stance, rolling his neck with a relaxed, lethal click.

Il-hyun rubbed his bruised throat, coughing hoarsely before letting out a dark, ragged chuckle.

"Was that supposed to be a honey trap?"

"Shut your mouth."

"Don't waste it on anyone else," Il-hyun rasped, his eyes gleaming with wicked amusement. "Save that routine exclusively for me."

Ja-kyeong launched forward without a word.

Il-hyun slipped the incoming jab, only for a vicious knee strike to drive toward his ribs. Blocking the impact with his forearm, Il-hyun tried to close the distance, but Ja-kyeong whipped the silk tie around Il-hyun's wrist, wrenching his arm into an agonizing hammerlock.

Il-hyun drove a heavy heel into the back of Ja-kyeong’s knee, simultaneously snapping his trapped wrist free.

The grapple broke, putting distance between them once more.

Limping slightly on his struck leg, Ja-kyeong wrapped the silk tightly around his right knuckles. He surged back in, trading a blistering flurry of parries and strikes until his right cross caught Il-hyun flush across the jawline.

CRACK.

Il-hyun’s head snapped sideways. His face darkened into a terrifying, murderous scowl.

He ran his tongue along the inside of his cheek, tasting warm, metallic iron. Turning his head, he spat a thick gob of crimson spit onto the floorboards.

When he looked back, Ja-kyeong was lightly beckoning with his fingers, wearing an infuriating, mocking smirk.

Il-hyun ground his teeth, a feral grin splitting his bruised lips.

"Darling... are we really doing this?"

Ignoring the taunt, Ja-kyeong launched a high roundhouse kick.

Il-hyun ducked under the arc, caught the extended ankle, clamped the leg firmly against his ribs, and hoisted Ja-kyeong clean onto his broad shoulder. Airborne and inverted, Ja-kyeong hammered rapid, heavy hammer-fists into Il-hyun's spine.

Unfazed by the blows, Il-hyun spun on his heel and slammed Ja-kyeong full-force onto the wooden dining table.

CRASH!

The solid table shattered down the center, sending Ja-kyeong crashing onto the debris.

Rolling to his feet, Ja-kyeong drew a heavy steak knife and a carving fork from the kitchen block, twirling the blades into a dual-wield reverse grip.

Il-hyun unfastened the cuff buttons of his dress shirt, rolling the sleeves past his forearms with a slow, measured exhale.

"Drop the cutlery. I'm on the verge of genuinely losing my temper."

"I'm the one who gets to be angry here," Ja-kyeong hissed. "Our account was settled twelve months ago."

"Settled by whose authority? You violated our terms. Did I ask you to put two bullets through my legs?"

"You put a kill order on my head the second the trigger was pulled! Did you think I was deaf?!"

Il-hyun put on a wounded, pouty expression. "I didn't actually kill you, did I?"

Jakyeong scoffed in pure disbelief. As if nearly having my skull ventilated just vanishes into thin air.

"So you dragged me here to finish the job?"

Taking in the boy's venomous, defensive posture, Il-hyun dropped his hands to his sides, letting out a tired sigh.

"If my objective was your execution, I would have put you in the dirt the moment my team tracked your coordinates. Your brother would be in a body bag, too."

Ja-kyeong’s jaw locked.

He hated to admit it, but the logic was sound. Over the past four days in isolation, he had turned the pieces over a hundred times; Kang Il-hyun hadn't brought him back to butcher him. And the taxidermy threat was pure psychological theater.

Then what the hell does he actually want?

The darkness in Il-hyun’s eyes softened into a deep, heavy gaze.

"You crossed my mind... from time to time."

"..."

"Quite frequently, in fact. Not that you'd ever believe me."

The confession sounded so much like an earnest romantic overture that Ja-kyeong’s face twisted into an expression of profound disgust.

Seeing the reaction, Il-hyun broke into his familiar, teasing purr. "Look at that... You're thrilled, aren't you?"

"Shut the fuck up and tell me the real reason," Ja-kyeong snapped.

A singular suspicion had been nagging at the back of his mind, though he had dismissed it as improbable. But watching the shift in Il-hyun's posture, the truth became undeniable.

Wiping the playful smirk from his face, Il-hyun laid the cards bare.

"I need you to handle a fresh assignment for me. Assuming, of course, you agree to the terms."

Fucking knew it.

Ja-kyeong kept his jaw clenched, glaring in silent contempt.

Right on cue, Il-hyun’s mobile phone chimed. He brought the receiver to his ear, exchanged a few brief, clipped instructions, and tucked the device away.

Meeting Ja-kyeong's guarded eyes, Il-hyun offered a bright, charming smile—the dark bruise blossoming along his jawline standing out in stark relief.

"Let's head up."

"Where?"

"Your brothers have arrived. They're waiting upstairs."
